title_en: Provisions of the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, and the Ministry of Justice on Legal Aid Work in Criminal Proceedings
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate, Ministry of Public Security, Ministry of Justice

Regulations on Legal Aid in Criminal Proceedings

(Sifa Tong [2005] No. 78)

Article 1 These Regulations are formulated in accordance with the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Lawyers Law of the People's Republic of China, the Legal Aid Regulations, and other relevant provisions, and in light of the actual work of legal aid, for the purpose of strengthening and regulating legal aid in criminal proceedings.

Article 2 Where a criminal suspect, a defendant in a public prosecution case, a victim in a public prosecution case and his or her legal representative or near relative, or a private prosecutor in a private prosecution case and his or her legal representative, due to financial difficulties, has not retained a lawyer or entrusted a litigation representative, he or she may apply for legal aid to the legal aid agency at the location of the public security organ, people's procuratorate, or people's court handling the case.

Where a criminal suspect or defendant is a person with limited capacity for civil conduct, his or her legal representative may apply for legal aid on his or her behalf.

Article 3 The standard for a citizen's financial difficulties shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government where the case is accepted.

Article 4 After the first interrogation of a criminal suspect according to law or from the date of adoption of compulsory measures, a public security organ or people's procuratorate shall, while informing the criminal suspect of his right to retain a lawyer to provide legal consultation, to file petitions or complaints on his behalf, or to apply for bail on his behalf, also inform him that if he has financial difficulties, he may apply for legal aid to a legal aid agency. For cases involving State secrets, the criminal suspect shall be informed that an application for legal aid must be approved by the investigative authority.

Within three days from the date of receiving the case materials transferred for examination and prosecution, a people's procuratorate shall, while informing the criminal suspect of his right to entrust a defender, also inform him that if he has financial difficulties, he may apply for legal aid to a legal aid agency; and while informing the victim and his or her legal representative or near relative of their right to entrust a litigation representative, also inform them that if they have financial difficulties, they may apply for legal aid to a legal aid agency.

Within three days from the date of completing the examination of a public prosecution case, a people's court shall, while informing the defendant of his right to entrust a defender, also inform him that if he has financial difficulties, he may apply for legal aid to a legal aid agency.

Within three days from the date of accepting a private prosecution case, a people's court shall, while informing the private prosecutor and his or her legal representative of their right to entrust a litigation representative, also inform them that if they have financial difficulties, they may apply for legal aid to a legal aid agency.

Article 5 The notification may be made orally or in writing. If made orally, a record shall be made and signed by the person notified; if made in writing, the receipt of service shall be placed in the case file.

Article 6 After receiving an application for legal aid from a detained criminal suspect or defendant, a public security organ, people's procuratorate, or people's court shall forward the application to the local legal aid agency within 24 hours, and notify the applicant's legal representative, near relative, or other person entrusted by the applicant to assist in providing the relevant certificates, documents, and case materials as stipulated in Article 17 of the Legal Aid Regulations.

If the address of the criminal suspect's legal representative or near relative is unknown and notification cannot be made, the public security organ, people's procuratorate, or people's court shall inform the legal aid agency of this when forwarding the application.

Article 7 After receiving an application, a legal aid agency shall promptly review it and make a decision in accordance with relevant provisions. If the applicant meets the conditions for legal aid, it shall decide to provide legal aid and, within three days from the date of the decision, assign a lawyer and notify the public security organ, people's procuratorate, or people's court by letter; if the applicant does not meet the conditions, it shall decide not to provide legal aid and, within three days from the date of the decision, inform the applicant in writing of the reasons and notify the public security organ, people's procuratorate, or people's court by letter.

The official letter on criminal legal aid issued by the legal aid agency shall state the name and contact information of the assigned lawyer.

Article 8 If an applicant disagrees with a legal aid agency's decision not to provide legal aid, he or she may raise an objection with the judicial administrative department that determines the legal aid agency. The judicial administrative department shall review the matter within five working days from the date of receiving the objection. If, upon review, it finds that the applicant meets the conditions for legal aid, it shall, in written form, order the legal aid agency to promptly provide legal aid to the applicant and notify the applicant at the same time. If it finds that the applicant does not meet the conditions, it shall uphold the legal aid agency's decision not to provide legal aid and inform the applicant in writing of its decision and the reasons thereof.

Article 9 Where a people's court appoints a defender in accordance with the Criminal Procedure Law and relevant judicial interpretations, it shall deliver the notice of appointment of defender and a copy of the indictment or a copy of the judgment to the legal aid agency at its location, which shall accept and organize the implementation uniformly.

If a people's court decides to hold a trial, it shall deliver the notice of appointment of defender and a copy of the indictment or a copy of the judgment to the legal aid agency at its location at least 10 days before the trial.

The notice of appointment of defender from the people's court shall state the nature of the case, the name of the defendant, the reasons for the appointment of a defender, the name and contact information of the person handling the case, and, if a trial date has been set, the time and place of the trial.

Article 10 A legal aid agency shall, at least three days before the trial, inform the people's court by letter of the name and contact information of the assigned person handling the case.

Article 11 After receiving the assignment from a legal aid agency, a lawyer shall promptly go through the entrustment procedures in accordance with relevant provisions.

For cases where the people's court appoints a defender, the lawyer shall, before the trial, ask the defendant whether he or she agrees to the lawyer acting as his or her defender. If the defendant disagrees, the lawyer shall record this in the case file and inform the people's court and the legal aid agency in writing.

Article 12 If a defendant insists on defending himself and refuses the lawyer appointed by the people's court to act as his defender, the people's court shall permit this and record it in the case file.

For a defendant who falls under circumstances where a defender must be appointed, the people's court shall ascertain the reasons for the refusal to appoint a defender. If there are legitimate reasons, it shall permit the refusal, but the defendant must entrust another defender. If the defendant does not entrust another defender, the people's court shall appoint another lawyer for him.

If the people's court decides to appoint another defender for the defendant in accordance with the preceding paragraph, it shall notify the legal aid agency that made the assignment by letter within three days from the date of the decision.

Article 13 When a circumstance as stipulated in Article 23 of the Legal Aid Regulations occurs in a criminal case where legal aid is being provided, the legal aid agency and the people's court shall, on the same day as making the decision to terminate legal aid or to terminate the appointment of a defender, notify the other party by letter, and the other party shall make a corresponding decision to terminate.

Article 14 If a people's court decides to change the trial time, it shall inform the lawyer handling the legal aid case at least three days before the trial. If the lawyer handling the legal aid case has legitimate reasons for being unable to appear in court on time, he or she may apply to the people's court for an adjournment. If the people's court agrees to the adjournment, it shall promptly notify the lawyer handling the legal aid case.

Article 15 For cases where the people's court decides not to hold a trial, the lawyer handling the legal aid case shall submit a written defense opinion to the people's court within 10 days from the day after receiving the assignment letter from the legal aid agency.

Article 16 Public security organs and people's procuratorates shall support the work of lawyers handling legal aid cases according to law. They shall inform the lawyer of the crimes suspected by the criminal suspect, arrange for the lawyer to meet the detained criminal suspect according to law, and provide necessary conveniences for the lawyer to provide legal consultation to the criminal suspect, to file petitions or complaints on his or her behalf, or to apply for bail for the detained criminal suspect.

Article 17 During the stage of examination and prosecution, a people's procuratorate shall provide conveniences for the lawyer handling the legal aid case to consult, extract, and copy the procedural documents and technical appraisal materials of the case, and to meet and correspond with the detained criminal suspect.

When examining a case, a people's procuratorate shall listen to the opinions of the lawyer handling the legal aid case.

Article 18 After a public security organ dismisses a case or transfers the case for examination and prosecution, and after a people's procuratorate initiates a public prosecution or makes a decision not to prosecute, it shall, within five days, inform the lawyer handling the legal aid case of the outcome of the case handling.

Article 19 A people's court shall support the work of lawyers handling legal aid cases according to law and provide conveniences for them to consult, extract, and copy the materials concerning the facts of the crime charged in the case, and to meet and correspond with the detained defendant.

Article 20 Public security organs, people's procuratorates, and people's courts shall waive or reduce the fees for lawyers handling legal aid cases to copy necessary relevant materials. The reduced fee standard shall be calculated based on the necessary cost of copying the materials.

Article 21 In the course of handling legal aid cases, lawyers shall perform their duties diligently and conscientiously, and abide by professional ethics and practice discipline.

Legal aid agencies shall provide professional guidance and supervision over the legal aid activities of lawyers to ensure the quality of legal aid cases.

If, during the handling of a case, a public security organ, people's procuratorate, or people's court discovers that a lawyer has violated professional ethics and practice discipline, thereby harming the interests of the aided person, it shall promptly notify the legal aid agency that made the assignment of the relevant circumstances.

Article 22 A people's court shall state in the judgment or ruling the legal aid agency that made the assignment, the lawyer handling the case, and the law firm to which the lawyer belongs.

Article 23 These Regulations shall take effect as of December 1, 2005. Where the Joint Notice on the Work of Criminal Legal Aid issued by the Supreme People's Court and the Ministry of Justice on April 9, 1997, the Joint Notice on Carrying Out Legal Aid Work in Criminal Proceedings issued by the Supreme People's Procuratorate and the Ministry of Justice on April 24, 2000, and the Joint Notice on Carrying Out Legal Aid Work in Criminal Proceedings issued by the Ministry of Justice and the Ministry of Public Security on April 25, 2001, conflict with these Regulations, these Regulations shall prevail.

September 28, 2005
